items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the Syracuse
regional airport
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8956

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the Syracuse
regional airport

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends the enabling legislation for the Syracuse Regional
Airport Authority to adjust the terms and obligations of board members.
It increases the term for rotating members from the Towns of Salina,
Cicero, Clay and North Syracuse School District from one to two years.
It authorizes a newly elected Mayor of Syracuse to replace an existing
mayoral appointee, the one with the shortest remaining term. It provides
that the removal of board members be made in accordance with Section
2827 of the Public Authorities Law, and that board members must comply
with the disclosure and ethics requirements of the Public Authorities
Law.

Section 2: Authorizes the Syracuse Regional Airport Authority to estab-
lish subsidiaries to assist in the operation of the Airport.

Section 3: Amends Section 2799-iii of the enabling legislation requiring
that the City of Syracuse approve capital projects at the Airport over
$10 million. It now requires that the City only be given notice.

Section 4: Increases the bonding limit of the Syracuse Regional Airport
Authority from $200,000,000 to $300,000,000.

Section 5: Establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Syracuse Regional Airport Authority ("Authority") was created by
statute in 2011 to improve and modernize the operation of the Hancock
International Airport ("Hancock") in Syracuse, NY. To date, the Authori-
ty has successfully managed the operation of the Airport and accom-
plished its goal of better coordinating air travel in Central New York.
Over the last decade, the Authority made extensive renovations and
improvements to Hancock's terminal and infrastructure and successfully
attracted new carriers to the Airport.

Now, with a decade of operating experience, the Authority has identified
a series of initiatives that will further improve operations and expand
services at Hancock. These require changes to the Authority's enabling
legislation and corresponding changes in State Law. Additionally,
current federal FAA regulations require certain changes to the Authori-
ty's operating structure.

The additional changes in the bill will provide the Authority with
greater staffing and financial flexibility to improve operations, make
capital improvements and ensure it stays fiscally sound.  Finally,
changes are being made to the governing structure of the Authority to
provide better conformity with the State's Public Authorities Law and
remove redundant and overlapping authority in certain areas.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New Bill (Amending Chapter 463 of 2011).

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Ninety days after it shall be come law.
